# Best portable power stations for camping

For most campers, a 250-500Wh unit is the sweet spot. It's light enough to carry and covers phones, lights, camera batteries and a CPAP for a weekend. Go bigger only if you want to run a fridge or cooler, or stay out for several days.

## Weekend tent or car camping (about 270-290Wh)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus, about $249.** This is PowerStationGearLab's top pick. It has 288Wh of LiFePO4, weighs 8.3 lb and puts out 300W. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2 on its own site, but the Plus is still sold through Amazon. [Review and Amazon link](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus, about $269-299.** It has 286Wh and a 600W inverter, twice the Jackery's, and you can expand it to 572Wh. It weighs about 9.9 lb. [Review and Amazon link](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300, about $199.** It has 288Wh, a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard version with an AC outlet, not the AC-less "DC" variant. [Review and Amazon link](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Bluetti EB3A, about $179 (budget).** It has 268Wh and a 600W inverter. Its app is basic. [Review and Amazon link](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

## Longer trips or a 12V fridge (about 1,000Wh and up)
- **Bluetti AC180, $499 ($474.05 with code AFF5OFF).** It has 1,152Wh, an 1,800W inverter, a 5-year warranty and weighs about 35 lb. It can't be expanded. [Buy at BLUETTI](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) (affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, about $799.** It has 1,070Wh and a 1,500W output. TechRadar picks it as best for camping. [TechRadar's list](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2, under $900 on sale (list $1,499).** OutdoorGearLab's top pick for multi-day off-grid camping. It weighs 39 lb, tops its lab tests with a score of 81, and in testing ran string lights, an electric cooler and device charging. [OutdoorGearLab review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

## Things to know
- Reviewers don't fully agree on the small units. OutdoorGearLab's lab scores for the Jackery 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) were fairly low, though it still calls the Jackery 300 its best buy for phones and laptops. The small-unit picks above come from PowerStationGearLab, so weigh them with that in mind.
- If you use a CPAP, turn the humidifier off. It can triple the machine's power draw.
- A folding solar panel lets you recharge on longer trips. Jackery panels pair most easily with Jackery units.
- Prices change often, and Black Friday is coming, so check the retailer page before you buy.

If you tell me what you'll run (CPAP, fridge, laptop) and how many nights you'll be out, I can narrow this to one pick.
